neighbours.label: efficacy words in claims about whether a medical treatment works (no better than, did not help, as effective as, little benefit); the + pole is the safety side (gentle, non-toxic)
fire: Several trials found the supplement no better than a sugar pill.
The review concluded that acupuncture was no more effective than placebo.
In most patients, the cream did not help clear the rash at all.
Doctors stress that antibiotics do not help a cold caused by a virus.
In the trial, the new drug worked no better than the standard treatment.
The study shows bed rest does not help back pain heal faster.
Honey turned out to be just as effective as cough syrup for children.
For many patients, the surgery offered little benefit over physical therapy.
quiet: Several trials found the supplement safe and well tolerated.
The review concluded that acupuncture was gentle and rarely painful.
In most patients, the cream left a faint smell on the skin.
Doctors stress that antibiotics should be taken with a full glass of water.
In the review, the new phone worked no better than the old model.
The gardener says extra water does not help tomatoes ripen faster.
Honey turned out to be sold in most pharmacies near the school.
For many patients, the surgery meant only a short stay in hospital.

notes: Probe: 'no better than sham surgery' 0.54, 'does not help relieve pain' 0.24, 'effectiveness' 0.17, 'benefit' 0.13, 'notice a difference' 0.09. Non-medical 'no better'/'does not help' 0.015-0.02, safety words 0.01-0.02. The median fire may be borderline.
